title: Natural Selection and Adaptation
seo_title: Natural Selection Worksheets: Adaptation, Resistance and Finch Beaks (High School Biology)
standard_text: Construct an explanation based on evidence that the process of evolution primarily results from four factors: (1) the potential for a species to increase in number, (2) the heritable genetic variation of individuals in a species due to mutation and sexual reproduction, (3) competition for limited resources, and (4) the proliferation of those organisms that are better able to survive and reproduce in the environment. Construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural selection leads to adaptation of populations.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on natural selection and adaptation (NGSS HS-LS4-2, HS-LS4-4): the four factors, peppered moths, antibiotic resistance and finch beak data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Individuals that survive and reproduce more pass their traits on, so populations adapt.
body_html:
How to think about it

Nature selects inherited traits that help survival.

  • Four factors: more offspring than can survive, inherited variation, competition for limited resources, and better-adapted individuals leaving more offspring.
  • Over many generations, the helpful trait becomes more common. That is an adaptation.
  • Individuals do not change to meet a need. Populations change because some individuals reproduce more.
Example

10,000 bacteria, 2% resistant. After the antibiotic?

2% of 10,000

Answer: 200 resistant bacteria

Example

Dark moths: 10% → 60% after soot. Why?

Dark moths hid from birds

Answer: they survived and reproduced more

Common mistakes

  • Thinking individuals change because they need to (Lamarck).
  • Thinking traits gained during life are inherited.
  • Thinking “survival of the fittest” means the strongest.

faq.q: What are the four factors of natural selection?
faq.a: More offspring than can survive, heritable variation, competition for limited resources, and better-adapted individuals surviving and reproducing more.
A few bacteria already have resistance genes. The antibiotic kills the others, so the resistant ones multiply and the population becomes resistant.
No. Individuals do not change their genes to meet a need. Populations evolve as helpful traits become more common over generations.

items.q: In England, soot darkened tree bark in the 1800s. Dark peppered moths became more common. Which explanation is best?
c: Dark moths were hidden from birds, so they survived and reproduced more.
The environment does not affect which individuals survive.
The moths turned dark because they needed to hide.
All individuals changed in the same way during their lives.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that are already present and inherited.

items.q: Moths that match the tree bark are eaten less and leave more offspring. Which factor of natural selection does this show?
c: better-adapted individuals survive and reproduce more
items.e: The four factors: overproduction, variation, competition and differential survival.

items.q: On dark lava rock, most rock pocket mice have dark fur. On light sand nearby, most have light fur. A student says: “The mice changed color to match where they live.” What is wrong with this claim?
c: Evolution is too slow to see.
Individuals do not change their genes to meet a need; selection acts on existing variation.
items.e: That is Lamarck's idea, not natural selection.
